title: finding(plugin-detail): `record-related-list.tsx` reads `relationshipValueField` through an `as any` cast, so the mirror declaration objectui#9469 adds does not reach the renderer's own read — the D1 shape, one renderer over
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, 2026-09-14T08:40Z, from the acceptance-notes residue of PR objectui#9469 (card objectui#8649). ⛔ Bare `finding` — no `domain:*`, no priority, no type, no assignee: routing and grading are triage's.

## Why this is a card and not an acceptance note

The implementing dev recorded it as an acceptance note with **`Carrier: none`**. ⭐ That is precisely the condition under which the acceptance-notes route does not hold: the test for that route is "name the PR or the person who will touch this file", and `none` fails it. So it is filed rather than left to be re-derived by whoever next opens the file.

## The reading

`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx` reads

```
(schema as any).relationshipValueField
```

— an explicit cast — for the very key PR objectui#9469 **declares** on `RecordRelatedListComponentProps` (`packages/types/src/record-components.ts`), aligning the mirror to `@objectstack/spec`'s `RecordRelatedListProps.relationshipValueField: z.string().default('id')`.

⇒ the declaration does not reach this renderer's own read. The cast unwraps it, exactly as the declaration-vs-cast defect that PR's contract review recorded as **D1** on a sibling renderer (`record-reference-rail.tsx`), and which that PR has since repaired there.

## ⚠️ Why the obvious dismissal is an argument, not a measurement

The dev's assessment, recorded as **the dev's reasoning rather than as a finding of this card**:

> it costs nothing (the mirror declaration exists so an external author's document compiles against the *published* type, which is measured and unaffected by the renderer's own read), and it is a behaviour-free one-token fix

That is probably right. ⛔ But D1 was an argument of the same shape — "the declaration is there, so the read is fine" — and it turned out to be a defect the moment an **expression** instrument was pointed at it rather than a **membership** one. The two instruments answer different questions:

- `getPropertyOfType` on the binding — a **membership** question. It unwraps casts, so it reports the key as declared either way.
- `getTypeAtLocation` on the read expression — an **expression** question. It is the only one that says what type the read actually carries.

⭐ The instrument that settles this card is the second. ⛔ It has not been run on this site by anyone: this card asserts the cast exists and asserts nothing about what the read's type is.

## What a repair would decide

1. Whether to drop the cast — `schema.relationshipValueField` — now that the declared member exists, and pin the read so a re-cast reddens. (⚠️ A regex pin is not enough: PR objectui#9469's own ledger assertion `toMatch(/properties\??\.entries/)` matched the cast and un-cast forms alike, which is why D1 survived a test.)
2. Or, if the cast is load-bearing for a reason not found here, say so at the site so the next reader does not file this again.

⚠️ Not measured: whether other renderers in `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/` carry the same cast-over-a-declared-key shape. This card names one site only; a census is the obvious first step of any repair and has not been run.

## Dedup

Searched this repo for the site and the shape; the instrument returned 4 results (so this is a live reading, not a dark zero) — objectui#7928, objectui#8883, objectui#8517, objectui#7299 — none about this cast or this key. Nothing open covers it.
